name: magic-ui-globe

frames.best_why: The sphere shows the most land and orange pins at once, with Africa and Europe filling the face.

tagline: A dotted globe turns slowly with orange pins on world cities.
summary: A WebGL globe of grey dots that spins on its own and can be dragged to turn it; small orange markers sit on chosen cities and the continents sweep past.
appearance: A sphere of dense grey dots forming the continents, set on a black stage under a large white-to-grey headline. Round orange pins sit on the surface at scattered places and the rim glows faintly.
behaviour: The globe turns steadily on its axis; dragging the sphere spins it and it eases to a stop on release. The cursor becomes a grab hand over it.
demo_content: The headline above the globe reads "Global edge".
use_when: A product wants to show worldwide reach behind a short headline.
avoid_when: A sized parent and WebGL are needed; without a graphics context it renders blank.
customise: A single config object sets colours, glow, the marker list, elevation and density; size and placement come from the parent and a class.
weight_why: A WebGL globe redrawn every animation frame in a requestAnimationFrame loop.

a11y.note: Drag to spin is pointer-only with no keyboard path, and the canvas has no text alternative describing the map.

polish_why: The dotted globe and orange pins read well and the drag feels right; the headline crowds the sphere.
title: Globe
